messages:
jamie: FYI billing alarm — big spike in GPU instance-hours in us-west2 over the last 2h. Console shows ~43 on-demand GPU nodes launched. anyone seeing autoscaler churn?

maria: I rolled a small autoscaler fallback change last week to allow cross-zone fallback when spot shortfall > 20% (to avoid capacity starvation). didn’t expect this many on-demand launches though. cc @rahul

rahul: can you paste the autoscaler policy? my guess: fallback logic picked the wrong node template in zone fallback (template for zone-b prefers a heavier GPU family).

jamie: here’s the scaledown/drain logs i grabbed from the cluster (redacted):
```
2026-05-18T09:12:04Z drain-hook: pre-drain script failed, exit=1 -> node not marked schedulable
2026-05-18T09:12:07Z autoscaler: launched instance groups us-west2-b (p4d-large) x12
2026-05-18T09:40:22Z autoscaler: spot shortage detected -> trigger cross-zone fallback
2026-05-18T09:41:11Z autoscaler: fallback template choose: zone-b-template (a100-large)
2026-05-18T10:03:50Z scale-in: nodes not drainable -> skip scale-in
```

alex: ah — drain hook failing causes the node to stay NotReady+cordoned so cluster-autoscaler won't remove it, and fallback kept provisioning additional capacity. do we have per-zone reserved capacity (commitments) in these zones?

maria: we have committed capacity in us-west2-a only. fallback provisioned in -b and -c where we have no commitments, so on-demand billing applies.

sophie: billing-bot shows a surge invoice for on-demand GPU hours starting 09:30 -> 11:45. estimate ~1200 GPU-hours. :grimacing:

billing-bot: alert: unplanned on-demand GPU spend detected. linked resources: compute-instance-group/us-west2-b, compute-instance-group/us-west2-c. Cost center: inference-prod.

rahul: timeline summary — spot eviction -> autoscaler fallback -> fallback picked wrong zone template -> drain hooks failed -> scale-in blocked -> many on-demand nodes accumulated.

jamie: action items i see: 1) rollback fallback policy to spot-only for critical pools (temporary), 2) fix drain-hook error (pre-drain script) and add alert for repeated pre-drain failures, 3) ensure fallback templates map to committed zones or smaller GPU families, 4) reconcile commitments vs actual zone usage with billing team.

maria: agree. i already opened a PR to add a canary check to the fallback selector so it won’t pick zone templates outside commitment zones. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/1245

alex: i'll patch the drain-hook quick fix now (it’s a timeout on kubectl cordon when apiserver hit a transient error). will also add a monotonic counter alert when drain-hook fails 3x in 15m.

sophie: i'll work with finance to flag the charge and start a credit request. need a precise list of instances and timestamps from cloud logs.

jamie: thanks. short-term rollback of fallback policy and a hotfix for the drain-hook is probably lowest risk. can someone own rollback? @maria?

maria: i can roll it back in the next 5m and post status.

ops-bot: deploy: rollback autoscaler-fallback-policy -> started by maria at 2026-05-18T10:05:02Z

maria: rolled back, monitoring for scale activity. cloud dashboard shows new launches stopped within 4m of rollback.

jamie: great. follow-ups: postmortem with root cause (template-zone mapping + missing commitment check) and cost impact estimate. i'll draft and share in #postmortems. thanks all. :thumbsup:
